reasoning_traces.think:
The means-end field encapsulates how organisms mentally structure environmental affordances into a navigable space of actions. Each arrow represents a potential path or relation between states: S (start), MO (means), and GO (goal). Succession hierarchy implies a directed acyclic graph where transitions follow a logical order. Mutual opposition arises when multiple paths from S to MO compete, suggesting a non-linear decision landscape. These primitives form a dual structure: one of ordered progression and another of competing alternatives. The failure mode emerges when either hierarchy breaks down due to environmental noise or opposition becomes too strong, causing agent to abandon rationality in favor of heuristics. This duality mirrors the mathematical concept of a category with both morphisms and co-morphisms, where the directionality of arrows defines the logic of choice while their multiplicity defines the complexity of deliberation.
